subject: mechanical
audience: FE Mechanical candidates and mechanical engineering students
title: The Refrigerator With a COP Greater Than One
featured_title: THE REFRIGERATOR WITH A COP GREATER THAN ONE

presentation.challenge: The refrigerator removed 6 kW of heat using 2 kW of work. A COP of 3 was correct, not impossible.

practice.primary_question: Why can a refrigerator have a coefficient of performance greater than 1 without violating energy conservation?
practice.typical_exam_trap: Treating refrigerator COP like thermal efficiency and assuming it cannot exceed 1.

case_dna.target_misconception: A refrigerator COP above 1 must violate energy conservation because no efficiency can exceed 100%.
case_dna.why_plausible: Thermal efficiency is dimensionless and bounded by 1, so COP can be mistakenly interpreted as the same metric.
case_dna.contradicting_evidence: If a refrigerator removes QL=6 kW while requiring W=2 kW, COP_R=QL/W=3. Energy balance gives QH=QL+W=8 kW, so energy is conserved.
case_dna.corrected_model: Refrigerator COP measures heat moved per unit work input, not the fraction of input energy converted to useful output. COP_R can exceed 1.

problem_statement: A refrigerator removes 6 kW of heat from a cold space while consuming 2 kW of electrical work. A reviewer rejects the calculated COP of 3 because it exceeds 1. Determine the correct COP and condenser heat rejection, then explain why the result does not violate the first law.

gates.label: Incident
gates.heading: The COP was 3. The first law was still satisfied.
facts: Heat removed from cold space: 6 kW

options.label: COP_R = QL/W and may exceed 1
options.reason: A refrigerator moves heat using work; it does not convert the work directly into the entire cooling load.

options.label: COP_R must be below 1 because all performance ratios are efficiencies
options.reason: COP and thermal efficiency are different performance measures.

options.label: COP_R = QL/QH
options.reason: Refrigerator COP uses work input in the denominator.

gates.label: Predict
gates.heading: Predict the refrigerator COP
gates.prompt: What is COP_R when QL=6 kW and W=2 kW?

gates.label: Gap
gates.heading: Close the energy balance
gates.prompt: Calculate the condenser heat rejection QH=QL+W in kW.
gates.success: QH=6+2=8 kW. The cycle moves 6 kW from the cold space and adds 2 kW of work before rejecting 8 kW.
gates.hint: Apply the first law to the complete refrigeration cycle.

gates.label: Evidence
gates.heading: COP above one does not create energy

cards.text: The refrigerator transfers 6 kW of existing thermal energy from the cold space.
The condenser rejects 6+2=8 kW, exactly satisfying the energy balance.

gates.label: Redline
gates.heading: Correct the performance review
report: C1. The refrigerator removes 6 kW from the cold space.
C2. It consumes 2 kW of work.
C3. A COP of 3 is impossible because performance ratios cannot exceed 1.

claims.label: C3
claims.reason: COP is not thermal efficiency; it measures heat moved per unit work.

evidence_choices.label: COP_R=6/2=3 and QH=6+2=8 kW
evidence_choices.reason: These equations show both valid performance and energy conservation.

correction.template: The refrigerator has COP={cop} and rejects {qh} kW at the condenser.

gates.label: Design Fix
gates.heading: Reduce work input for the same 6 kW cooling load

options.label: Improve the cycle to COP=4, reducing work input to 1.5 kW
Reduce COP to 2
options.reason: Then W=3 kW, which increases input power.

options.label: Force condenser heat rejection to equal only 6 kW
options.reason: That would omit the work input from the first-law balance.

gates.label: Transfer
gates.heading: Apply refrigerator COP
gates.prompt: A refrigerator removes 10 kW using 2.5 kW of work. What is COP_R?

options.reason: That adds heat and work instead of taking their ratio.

gates.explanation: Refrigerator COP is cooling load divided by required work input.

gates.label: Sign Off
gates.heading: Sign off the refrigeration balance
gates.confirmation: I confirm that refrigerator COP can exceed one because it measures heat transported per unit work input rather than conversion efficiency.

items.label: What failed
items.value: COP was interpreted as if it were a thermal efficiency.

items.label: What was missed
items.value: The refrigerator moves heat in addition to consuming work.

seo.seo_title: Refrigerator COP Greater Than 1: Why COP 3 Is Valid | FE E-053
seo.meta_description: Solve FE Mechanical Case E-053: a refrigerator removes 6 kW using 2 kW of work, giving COP 3 and rejecting 8 kW.
seo.excerpt: Refrigerator COP is not the same as thermal efficiency. A COP above one can be completely consistent with the first law.
seo.direct_answer: Refrigerator COP is QL/W. Removing 6 kW with 2 kW of work gives COP_R=3. The condenser rejects QH=QL+W=8 kW, so energy is conserved even though COP exceeds 1.

faqs.q: Can refrigerator COP be greater than 1?
faqs.a: Yes. COP measures heat moved per unit work input, not conversion efficiency.

faqs.q: If QL=6 kW and W=2 kW, what heat is rejected?
